- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for 1–3 day leads.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust downward by 1–3% if recent 5–7 day average is below 3σ of historical volatility.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes (even if sentiment = 0.00); apply a 1–3% dampening factor to forecast peaks if preceded by 3+ consecutive days of high volatility.
- If sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), assume no directional bias; apply a 1–2% downward correction to forecast mean if 3+ consecutive days show upward trend in price.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid overconfidence in late-period spikes; cap forecast values at 10–15% below the 30-day true outcome’s 90th percentile if sentiment remains neutral.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after forecast peak, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid “over-leverage” bias.
